name: Sherwin-Williams
headline: Paint sold to contractors through its own 4,853 stores, where rivals' stores earned little.
what_short: Paint, coatings and company-owned paint stores
what_it_does: Sherwin-Williams makes paint and coatings and sells most of the architectural paint itself, through 4,853 company-operated stores in the US, Canada and the Caribbean. These mainly serve painting contractors and do-it-yourself homeowners. It also sells brands such as Valspar, Minwax and Krylon through home centres and dealers, and industrial coatings worldwide.
why_it_passed: Its paint stores made $3.06 billion of pre-tax income on $13.6 billion of sales in 2025, a 22.5% margin, and the store margin has widened from 13% to 22%.
A competitor, PPG, ran paint stores that earned only 1% to 4% and sold them at a loss, which shows how hard the model is to copy.
Its prices rose in every year the analysis read, which indicates pricing power.
Before tax it earned very high returns on the tangible capital it needs: 71% in 2018, for example (84% before amortizing acquired intangibles).
why_not_now: At $318.46 a share the price is above the top of the analysis's value range of $140 to $225. The expected return at that price is about 3% to 5% a year before tax, below the 5.66% a 30-year US Treasury bond pays, and the price already assumes about 10% a year cash growth.
watch: It has bought back shares at prices above the analysis's value range, and partly with borrowed money in 2026.
Its company reports lean on EBITDA and adjusted earnings, which the analysis treats as flattering.
Old lead-pigment litigation is named among its risks, and $1.5 billion of long-term debt was due within a year.
